gap: No result ChatGPT got states a like-for-like named CPU measurement across its picks. In PassMark's CPU Mark the UGREEN DXP2800's N100 scores 5,305, the N5095 in the TerraMaster F2-423 and F2-425 scores 4,003 (32.5% lower), the J4125 in the Synology DS225+ scores 2,927 (45% lower) and the N95 in the Beelink ME Mini scores 5,278. None of those results gives any measured power or noise figure for the F2-425 or the Beelink ME Mini either.
standout_why: I opened TechRadar's F2-424 review (cited), but only its title came back, so I have no figures from it. The others I read were verdictbits /reviews/best-nas-for-homelab/ (rank 4, not cited), bitdoze /best-nas-homelab-docker-proxmox/, rottenwifi's DXP2800 review and starryhope /nas/best-budget-nas/. Verdictbits already gives igor'sLAB's idle figures for the DXP2800 (5.6 W) and F2-424 (8.5 W), and starryhope gives OCinside's 7 W for the DXP2800. So rival pages already cover DXP2800 idle power. None of the rival pages has a CPU benchmark comparing N100, N5095, J4125 and N95. None has a named measurement for the F2-423, F2-425, Beelink ME Mini or DS225+. Bitdoze has no measurements at all. Rottenwifi gives only ComputerBase's verdict in words.
decides: This confirms the DXP2800 as the pick for a Docker and VM learner. It has about 33% more CPU than the cheaper TerraMaster F2-423/F2-425 that ChatGPT suggested, which also ship with half the RAM (4 GB DDR4). It has 81% more CPU than the DS225+ we list. The Beelink ME Mini's N95 essentially matches the N100 on CPU (5,278 vs 5,305). The DIY Life measured the N150 ME Mini at about 8 W idle with two NVMe drives. That makes the ME Mini a real equal for an SSD-only plain-Linux lab, but it has no 3.5-inch bays. The F2-425's 11–12 W idle with two SSDs (Hardware Busters) is roughly double the DXP2800's 5.6 W SSD-only figure (igor'sLAB), and the F2-425 is the slower machine.
